p.x:
A common sentiment heard in AI discourse is that "In order to predict the next token you need to accurately model the world" but this is of course not true!

Looking at humans: We begin with our own judgments of relevance.
From these we build an artificial system (language) that merely correlates with those judgments; it is not how the world itself works.

On top of language we construct a second artificial layer: literacy, whose patterns are again correlated with language. If you can predict literacy, you can usually predict language, and indirectly say something useful about the world, because language tracks our sense of relevance.

However, these machines never predict the world directly. They predict how we would talk about our anticipation of the world. That crucial indirection explains why they cannot, for instance, generalize to explain a chimp’s intelligence: chimps don’t gain their intelligence by guessing how they’ll describe their own anticipations.

p.x:
When did people stop dancing? 

I was just on a rooftop with about 200 people, amazing DJ, and I was one of maybe 3 people doing anything with my limbs. At most of the raves and clubs have been to in the past few years, me and my friends have been in the minority for doing more movement than swaying back and forth and bouncing our heads in a distracted way. Wth?! Why are people even on the dance floor to begin with if not to dance? 

I wondered if not-dancing has become the “cool” thing, but that doesn’t seem it. When someone starts actually dancing, the  people around them seem happy, like “oh, now I have permission to bob my head a little more and smile.”

One theory is that [doing anything that might get posted online and then get attacked] has dominated the urban American psyche. 

But I wonder if it’s more due to the rise and fall of various party drugs. Amongst adults ages 19-30, use of stimulant party drugs like MDMA and cocaine have decreased. Meanwhile, use of relaxants like cannabis and ketamine have increased. At the same time, young people are drinking less alcohol, a substance which often disinhibits people to let loose.

Personally, I tend to dance sober, but I miss the dance floors of the 2010s. Maybe the miracle of modern science can invent some kind of new party drug that has minimal harmful effects to get people dancing again. 

Anyway, what do you guys think is going on?

p.x:
Even when I was a child, I wasn’t inclined to go complain or cry to my parents when I had a problem. Not sure why. Maybe because we were new to America, and my mother was often uncomfortable and scared, standoffish from a society that wasn’t very welcoming, and I intuited that her norms weren’t compatible with the ones I needed to learn. Maybe I’m just hard-headed and independent by nature. It’s hard to say.

When I got older, I started to notice how grounding my parents could be in the moments when I’d really given up on myself. Not always, but often, they’d remind me to have faith not even in myself, but in God, and to find self-belief through the almighty that made me, that continues to love me. Only rarely have they responded to me sharing an issue by amplifying the crisis — they’re far more likely to panic about a tough choice I’m making knowingly than a mistake I’ve already made, and I’m lucky for that.

But I’m at the age now where I don’t see my parents that often. Every few months, which is more frequent than most adults who live thousands of miles away see their families, but it doesn’t feel like enough for any of us, although I’m reticent to admit that to them. They’d rather I live upstairs in their house than any of the places I’ve been for the last many years. And now, in moments when I really feel like I don’t wanna be irredeemable, or I might need an endless nap, and I would kill for my dad’s chai and my mom’s food and a hug from both of them, I can’t even get myself to call them. I don’t want them to hear the pain in my voice. I don’t want to worry them. 

So instead I cry in public. And I listen to their voicemails and cry more. And I ignore their calls, text them that I’m busy, sorry! And I wonder if a few decades from now, my kids will do the same to me. And I try not to lose faith that one day I’ll even have the opportunity to be betrayed by my children the way I betray them. I feel like I’m the worst, but I think they’re still glad they have me.
